title: NY State Assembly · District 31
area: Southeast Queens and the Rockaway Peninsula, including Arverne, Brookville, Far Rockaway, Hammels, Rosedale, South Ozone Park, South Richmond Hill, Springfield Gardens, and John F. Kennedy International Airport

context.text: Khaleel Anderson's Democratic and Working Families Party primaries, both scheduled for June 23, 2026, were canceled because he had no primary opponent; he advanced on both lines without appearing on the ballot. No Republican candidate qualified for the general election ballot.

summary.text: Khaleel Anderson is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party Assembly member for District 31 in southeast Queens, first elected in a 2020 special election. He is running unopposed in the November 3, 2026 general election.

background.text: Anderson was born in Brooklyn, New York, and lives in Far Rockaway, Queens.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Queens College in 2019.

Before his election, his career experience included working as a community organizer, including youth civic-engagement organizing beginning at age 13 and helping build a half-acre urban farm that provided fresh produce, job training, and workshops.
He was the youngest member of Queens Community Board 14 and of his local Police Precinct Council prior to taking office.
Anderson won a 2020 special election to the Assembly at age 24, becoming the youngest Black state lawmaker in New York history.

priorities.text: Anderson describes his campaign vision as "A New Fight Together," an "intergenerational and culturally diverse coalition of working-class people advocating for lasting progressive change in Assembly District 31."
priorities.quote: Our vision of A New Fight Together is an intergenerational and culturally diverse coalition of working-class people advocating for lasting progressive change in Assembly District 31.

priorities.text: He lists his issue priorities as criminal justice reform, addressing the housing crisis, transportation justice, healthcare for all, environmental justice, education, and jobs and economic development.
He states his overall goal as building "a state that educates our children, cares for our elders, and provides a safe, healthy and prosperous community for all."
priorities.quote: We will work for a state that educates our children, cares for our elders, and provides a safe, healthy and prosperous community for all of us.

positions.summary: Sponsored "Francesco's Law," which creates violations for failing to safely store firearms around minors or prohibited persons, and separately sponsored bills to create a state database on microstamped guns and to criminalize possession of ghost guns.

Lists "Healthcare For All" among his campaign issue pages and, during the COVID-19 pandemic, called for expanded testing, income support, and hazard pay, saying the community lacked equal, quality health care.
positions.quote: We don't have equal health care. We don't get quality care. And many of us-even now-get no care.

positions.summary: Sponsored legislation to establish a "Green New Deal for New York" task force and lists environmental justice as a campaign priority.

Sponsored NYCHA-focused tenant-protection legislation, including a bill addressing mold remediation in NYCHA housing and a bill establishing a NYCHA utility accountability act, and lists "Addressing the Housing Crisis" as a campaign priority.

record.text: Sponsored "Francesco's Law" (A.1962), which creates violations for failing to safely store rifles, shotguns, and firearms around minors or prohibited persons. The bill passed the Assembly on June 11, 2025 and again on May 13, 2026, and passed the Senate on June 2, 2026, after being returned to the Assembly.

Sponsored A.9083, which would require the Metropolitan Transportation Authority to establish a 30-day fare-cap program giving riders an unlimited pass after paying a set amount in fares; as of January 2026 it remained referred to the Assembly Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee.

Sponsored A.8686, which would authorize the state Department of Health to designate a Level 1 or Level 2 trauma center in Far Rockaway, Queens; as of January 2026 it remained referred to the Assembly Health Committee.
Sponsored A.5096, which would withhold the governor's salary until the state budget is passed; as of January 2026 it remained referred to the Assembly Governmental Operations Committee.

Chairs the Assembly Task Force on Food, Farm & Nutrition Policy and serves as a member of the Children and Families, Energy, Environmental Conservation, Insurance, Labor, and People with Disabilities committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Voted yes on S.6954-B, requiring providers of synthetic content creation systems to include content-provenance disclosures; the bill passed the Assembly 141-0 on an unspecified 2026 session date.
